aspnetcore-problemdetails-api-errors.title: Standardize ASP.NET Core API errors with ProblemDetails
aspnetcore-problemdetails-api-errors.short: Return failures from HTTP APIs in a consistent shape
aspnetcore-problemdetails-api-errors.summary: ProblemDetails represents HTTP API errors with common fields such as status, title, and detail and integrates with exception handling.
aspnetcore-problemdetails-api-errors.why: A shared error shape is easier for clients to consume than unrelated custom JSON payloads from every endpoint.
aspnetcore-problemdetails-api-errors.tips: Do not expose internal exceptions or secrets directly in detail; separate diagnostics from information intended for API consumers.

benchmarkdotnet-memory-diagnoser.title: Measure both speed and allocations with BenchmarkDotNet
benchmarkdotnet-memory-diagnoser.short: Avoid judging small performance differences with a hand-written Stopwatch loop
benchmarkdotnet-memory-diagnoser.summary: BenchmarkDotNet manages warmup and repeated measurements, while MemoryDiagnoser reports allocation behavior alongside execution time.
benchmarkdotnet-memory-diagnoser.why: JIT, GC, and warmup effects make one-shot timing especially easy to misread when evaluating optimizations.
benchmarkdotnet-memory-diagnoser.tips: Use representative inputs and inspect distributions and allocations rather than relying on a single mean value.

unity-update-allocation.title: Avoid per-frame allocations in Unity Update loops
unity-update-allocation.short: Keep temporary LINQ results and fresh lists out of hot frame paths
unity-update-allocation.summary: Repeated temporary allocations in Update and similar per-frame paths accumulate into GC pressure that can affect frame time.
unity-update-allocation.why: Even small allocations become significant when repeated dozens of times per second and can cause periodic collection stalls.
unity-update-allocation.tips: Use the Unity Profiler to confirm GC Alloc first, then reuse buffers or non-allocating APIs on genuinely hot paths.

dependency-injection-keyed-services.title: Select multiple implementations with keyed dependency injection services
dependency-injection-keyed-services.short: Attach keys to DI registrations when one service type has distinct implementations
dependency-injection-keyed-services.summary: Keyed Services let .NET dependency injection register multiple implementations for the same service type and resolve one by key.
dependency-injection-keyed-services.why: They can express named or purpose-specific implementations without centralizing selection in a large switch or service locator.
dependency-injection-keyed-services.tips: Do not scatter key strings throughout the application; prefer ordinary polymorphism and normal DI when they already model the choice well.

httpclient-standard-resilience-handler.title: Add a standard resilience pipeline to HttpClient
httpclient-standard-resilience-handler.short: Configure retries, timeouts, and related policies with the HTTP client
httpclient-standard-resilience-handler.summary: The standard handler from Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience provides a composed set of HTTP resilience strategies such as retries, timeouts, and circuit breaking.
httpclient-standard-resilience-handler.why: Central configuration is easier to reason about than writing a separate retry loop at every call site.
httpclient-standard-resilience-handler.tips: Do not blindly retry non-idempotent requests; account for server limits, Retry-After, and the total time budget.
